title: Renewed Request of Oracle Corporation for Expedited Issuance of Order re the Green Chile Project under CP26-80.

documents.name: Oracle Request for Expedited Authorization.pdf
documents.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

                                                         )
Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC                       )                    Docket No. CP26-80-000
                                                         )

                 RENEWED REQUEST OF ORACLE CORPORATION FOR
                    EXPEDITED ISSUANCE OF AUTHORIZATION

        On May 4, 2026, Oracle Corporation (“Oracle”) filed a request with the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”) seeking expedited review and approval of

Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC’s (“Transwestern”) prior notice request for the Green Chile

Project (the “Pipeline Project”).1 As previously noted in the Request, the Pipeline Project is

essential to delivering natural gas to a power plant that will supply electricity to one of the most

important data center campuses (“Project Jupiter”) in the United States, providing a dedicated

microgrid that leverages innovative fuel cell technology to power large-scale data center operations

while avoiding stress on the larger transmission and distribution system.

        Since the Request was filed, the Commission issued an environmental assessment (“EA”)

for the Pipeline Project,2 federal and state agencies have provided necessary concurrences,3 and

numerous parties have provided comments on the Pipeline Project. With the EA comment period



1
    Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC, Request of Oracle Corporation for Expedited Issuance of Order, Docket
    No. CP26-80-000 (May 4, 2026) (“Request”).
2
    Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC, Green Chile Project Environmental Assessment, Docket No. CP26-80-
    000 (Sept. 4, 2026); see also Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC, Notice of Availability of the Environmental
    Assessment for the Proposed Green Chile Project, Docket No. CP26-80-000 (Sept. 4, 2026) (providing for a 30-
    day comment period on the environmental assessment).
3
    See Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC, BLM Determination of Effect for the Green Chile Project, Docket No.
    CP26-80-000 (June 30, 2026) (Letter from the Bureau of Land Management [“BLM”] providing determination
    of “no historic properties affected”); see also Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC, Supplemental Agency
    Correspondence, Docket No. CP26-80-000 (Sept. 29, 2026) (Letter from the New Mexico Historic Preservation
    Division “concur[ring] with the BLM’s determination of No Adverse Effect for the Green Chile Pipeline
    Project.”).
 now closed, and Transwestern having already provided its responses to the comments on the EA,4

there are no additional procedural steps necessary in order for the Commission to authorize the

Pipeline Project. In this regard, Oracle hereby renews its request for expedited authorization of

the Pipeline Project, and urges the Commission to issue an order on the Pipeline Project as soon

as possible.


       I.      Project Jupiter is Creating Jobs.

       To date, 1,230 New Mexico residents, including 630 from Doña Ana County, where Project

Jupiter is located, have worked on Project Jupiter. Across the trades, more than 1,846 union

members have contributed to the project, and 4,393 workers have completed more than 3.75

million labor hours. For many of those workers, the project has made it possible to stay local

instead of traveling out of the county or the state to remain employed. At the peak of construction,

Project Jupiter is projected to support nearly 5,800 jobs across Doña Ana County. Once fully

operational, the campus is expected to support more than 3,100 jobs across the county, including

1,500 direct operational jobs at the campus. Those jobs are projected to generate $180 million in

annual pay and benefits. Moreover, these larger employment benefits will extend beyond the

campus. Project Jupiter is expected to support jobs in banking, insurance, maintenance, and other

business services, as well as in restaurants, retail, hospitality, and other local businesses. Project

Jupiter is bringing thousands of good, high-paying jobs, both directly and indirectly, to the Doña

Ana region.




4
    See Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC, Response to Comments on the Environmental Assessment, Docket
    No. CP26-80-000 (Oct. 13, 2026).

                                                   2
         II.      Project Jupiter is Driving Investment.

        During the 2025–28 construction period, Project Jupiter is projected to generate up to $1.1

billion in annual economic output in Doña Ana County. Once the four-building campus is fully

operational, its estimated annual economic impact is projected to total as much as $886 million,

including $560 million in direct economic impact. These projected benefits build on substantial

contributions already being delivered. To date, Project Jupiter has generated more than $100

million in state and local tax revenue, including $50 million delivered for local water

infrastructure. Its commitments also include $360 million to support schools, infrastructure, and

public services, and $6.9 million for workforce development and community programs. Project

Jupiter is supporting both immediate economic activity and lasting investments in the community.


        III.     Timely Approval of the Pipeline Project Ensures These Benefits Continue.

        As explained above, the Pipeline Project is essential to delivering the natural gas needed to

generate electricity for Oracle’s Project Jupiter.5 Timely completion of the Pipeline Project is

therefore critical to bringing the campus into operation and realizing the projected long-term

benefits for the Doña Ana County region that are discussed above. Time remains of the essence.

Delay in approving the Pipeline Project threatens to delay Project Jupiter’s operations and the

resulting jobs, economic activity, and community benefits.




5
    See also supra n.1, at 1–3.

                                                 3
        IV.    Conclusion.

       In light of the foregoing, Oracle renews its request for expedited authorization of the

Pipeline Project, and urges the Commission to issue an order on the Pipeline Project as soon as

possible.


 Dated: October 13, 2026                          Respectfully submitted,


                                                  /s/ Josh Pitcock_______
                                                  Josh Pitcock

                                                  Oracle Corporation
